setting: A small Italian bar (café counter) near Piazza Navona in Rome, mid-morning, not busy. The tutor is the barista behind the counter; the learner has just walked in and is ordering for themselves and a friend.

goal.en: Greet the barista and politely order a milky coffee.
goal.ko: 인사하고 우유 들어간 커피를 정중하게 주문하세요.

expect.meaning: greets and orders a cappuccino or another coffee
match: buongiorno, vorrei un cappuccino, per favore

goal.en: Ask politely for a drink.
Say you want two: one is for a friend.
Say that's all and ask how much it is.

expect.meaning: says nothing else, without asking the price

goal.en: Hand over the money and thank them.

expect.meaning: did not catch the price and asks again

goal.en: Say goodbye and that you'll see them soon.
goal.ko: 작별 인사를 하고 또 오겠다고 하세요.

expect.meaning: only says goodbye or returns the wish

hello.text: Buongiorno! Cosa le preparo?

gloss.en: Good morning! What can I make for you?
Good morning. What will you have?
Go ahead, tell me.

what-easy.text: Cosa prende? Un caffè? Un cappuccino?

gloss.en: What will you have? A coffee? A cappuccino?

menu.text: Abbiamo caffè, cappuccino, tè e spremuta d'arancia.

gloss.en: We have coffee, cappuccino, tea and fresh orange juice.
gloss.ko: 커피, 카푸치노, 차, 생오렌지 주스가 있어요.

gloss.en: Coffee, tea or orange juice.
Sure. One or two?
How many? One?
Here you are. Anything else?
Anything else? Yes or no?

price.text: Sono un euro e ottanta l'uno.

gloss.en: They're one euro eighty each.

price-easy.text: Uno e ottanta. Per ogni cappuccino.

gloss.en: One eighty. For each cappuccino.
Thank you. Have a good day!
Thanks. Have a good day!
See you soon!

setting: Piazza Duca d'Aosta, just outside Milano Centrale station, early afternoon. The learner has stopped a friendly local passer-by to ask the way to the metro.

goal.en: Say excuse me and ask where the metro is.
goal.ko: 실례한다고 하고 지하철이 어디 있는지 물어보세요.

match: scusi, dov'è la fermata della metro?
sì, dov'è la metro, per favore?

expect.meaning: asks whether there is a metro nearby

goal.en: It was too fast. Ask them to say it again, please.
goal.ko: 너무 빨랐어요. 다시 말해 달라고 부탁하세요.

match: può ripetere la strada, per favore?

goal.en: Ask if there is a pharmacy near here too.

expect.meaning: asks if there is a pharmacy nearby
match: grazie. c'è una farmacia qui vicino?
e c'è una farmacia qui vicino?

goal.en: Thank them for their help.

hello.text: Sì? Posso aiutarla?

gloss.en: Yes? Can I help you?
Do you need help?

dir.text: Allora, vada dritto e poi prenda la seconda a destra.

gloss.en: So, go straight on and then take the second on the right.
gloss.ko: 자, 쭉 가다가 두 번째 길에서 오른쪽으로 가세요.

gloss.en: Straight on. Then right.

slow.text: Certo. Dritto... poi la seconda a destra. Cinque minuti.

gloss.en: Sure. Straight on... then the second on the right. Five minutes.
gloss.ko: 그럼요. 쭉… 그다음 두 번째 길에서 오른쪽. 5분이요.

slow-easy.text: Sempre dritto, poi a destra. Cinque minuti.

gloss.en: Straight on, then right. Five minutes.

ok.text: Esatto, è facile. Le serve altro?

gloss.en: Exactly, it's easy. Do you need anything else?
gloss.ko: 맞아요, 쉬워요. 또 필요한 거 있어요?

gloss.en: Do you have another question?

pharmacy.text: Sì, c'è una farmacia proprio accanto alla metro.

gloss.en: Yes, there's a pharmacy right next to the metro.
gloss.ko: 네, 지하철 바로 옆에 약국이 있어요.

gloss.en: Yes. Near the metro.
All right. Have a good day!
OK. Goodbye!
Not at all! Goodbye.

setting: A small souvenir and leather shop near Ponte Vecchio in Florence, late morning. The tutor is the shop assistant. The learner wants a postcard and notices a small leather item next to the postcards.

goal.en: Say politely that you'd like a postcard.

expect.meaning: says they would like a postcard
match: buongiorno, vorrei una cartolina, per favore

goal.en: Point at the thing next to the postcards and ask what it is.
goal.ko: 엽서 옆의 물건을 가리키며 뭔지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: guesses what it is or what it is made of

goal.en: Say yes, you like it.
Ask how much it costs.

expect.meaning: asks about the price another way

goal.en: Say you'll take it.
Say you don't need a bag, thanks.

hello.text: Buongiorno! Cerca qualcosa?

gloss.en: Good morning! Are you looking for something?
Good morning. Do you need something?

cards.text: Certo, le cartoline sono qui. E guardi questo, è tipico.

gloss.en: Sure, the postcards are here. And look at this, it's typical.
gloss.ko: 그럼요, 엽서는 여기 있어요. 그리고 이거 보세요, 여기 특산이에요.

cards-easy.text: Le cartoline sono qui. E guardi questo.

gloss.en: The postcards are here. And look at this.

browse.text: Prego, faccia pure. Lì ci sono le cartoline, e questo è molto tipico.

gloss.en: Please, go ahead. The postcards are there, and this is very typical.
gloss.ko: 네, 천천히 보세요. 저기 엽서가 있고, 이건 아주 이곳다운 거예요.

what.text: È un segnalibro di pelle, fatto qui a Firenze. Le piace?

gloss.en: It's a leather bookmark, made here in Florence. Do you like it?
gloss.ko: 가죽 책갈피예요, 여기 피렌체에서 만들었어요. 마음에 드세요?

what-easy.text: È un segnalibro, di pelle. Le piace?

gloss.en: It's a bookmark, made of leather. Do you like it?

what-yes.text: Sì, di pelle! È un segnalibro, fatto a Firenze. Le piace?

gloss.en: Yes, leather! It's a bookmark, made in Florence. Do you like it?
gloss.ko: 네, 가죽이에요! 피렌체에서 만든 책갈피예요. 마음에 드세요?

nice.text: Bello, vero? E non è caro.

gloss.en: Nice, isn't it? And it isn't expensive.
It's nice. It doesn't cost much.

other.text: Va bene. Ci sono altri colori, guardi.

gloss.en: All right. There are other colours, look.
Look: there are other colours.

price.text: Il segnalibro costa otto euro, la cartolina un euro.

gloss.en: The bookmark costs eight euros, the postcard one euro.

price-easy.text: Otto euro il segnalibro. Un euro la cartolina.

gloss.en: Eight euros the bookmark. One euro the postcard.
Perfect. Would you like a bag?
A bag? Yes or no?

end.text: Ecco a lei. Grazie e arrivederci!

gloss.en: Here you are. Thank you and goodbye!

setting: The front desk of a small family-run hotel near the Rialto in Venice, early evening. The tutor is the receptionist. The learner has a booking for two nights under the name Kim.

goal.en: Say good evening and that you have a booking.
goal.ko: 저녁 인사를 하고 예약이 있다고 하세요.

match: ho una prenotazione per due notti

goal.en: Tell them your name.
Say yes, that's right.
Ask where the lift is.

expect.meaning: asks where the lift or room is

match: a che ora è la colazione?

goal.en: Ask what time breakfast is.

match: a che ora è la colazione?
e la colazione, a che ora?

goal.en: Thank them and say good night.

hello.text: Buonasera! Benvenuti all'Hotel Laguna. Mi dica.

gloss.en: Good evening! Welcome to Hotel Laguna. How can I help?
gloss.ko: 안녕하세요! 라구나 호텔에 오신 걸 환영해요. 말씀하세요.

gloss.en: Good evening. Did you book a room?
Good evening! Do you have a booking?
Did you book? Yes or no?
Very good. What's your name?
Your name, please?

nights.text: Kim... Ah, sì, eccola. Due notti, giusto?

gloss.en: Kim... Ah yes, here it is. Two nights, right?
gloss.ko: 김… 아, 네, 여기 있네요. 2박 맞죠?

gloss.en: Two nights, right?

key.text: Perfetto. Ecco la chiave: camera dodici.

gloss.en: Perfect. Here's the key: room twelve.
Here's the key. Room twelve.

change.text: Ah, mi scusi! Ora va bene. Ecco la chiave: camera dodici.

gloss.en: Oh, I'm sorry! Now it's right. Here's the key: room twelve.

lift.text: È lì, a sinistra. La camera è al secondo piano.

gloss.en: It's there, on the left. The room is on the second floor.
On the left. Second floor.

breakfast.text: La colazione è dalle sette alle dieci, al primo piano.

gloss.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten, on the first floor.
From seven to ten.
You're welcome! Have a nice evening.
Good night, and enjoy your stay!

setting: The first evening of an Italian course for foreigners in Bologna, in the break before class starts. The tutor is Chiara, a friendly classmate from Naples who works as a museum guide.

goal.en: Say hello and tell her your name.

expect.meaning: gives their name in a shorter way

goal.en: Say which city you're from.
Say what you are: you're at university.
Ask her the same question back.
goal.ko: 그 사람에게도 같은 걸 되물어 보세요.

goal.en: Say it was nice to meet her.

expect.meaning: says it was nice to meet

hello.text: Ciao! Io sono Chiara. E tu come ti chiami?

gloss.en: Hi! I'm Chiara. And what's your name?
gloss.ko: 안녕! 나는 키아라야. 너는 이름이 뭐야?

gloss.en: I'm Chiara. And you?
Nice to meet you, Minji! Where are you from?

from-easy.text: Di dove sei? Di che città?

gloss.en: Where are you from? Which city?

city.text: Che bello! E cosa fai? Studi o lavori?

gloss.en: How nice! And what do you do? Do you study or work?
gloss.ko: 멋지다! 그럼 무슨 일 해? 공부해, 아니면 일해?

gloss.en: Do you study? Or work?

korea.text: Ah, dalla Corea! E cosa fai? Studi o lavori?

gloss.en: Ah, from Korea! And what do you do? Do you study or work?
gloss.ko: 아, 한국에서 왔구나! 그럼 무슨 일 해? 공부해, 일해?

gloss.en: Ah, you study! How nice.
Good!
Ah, you work! Interesting.
Ah, good!

me.text: Io lavoro in un museo, sono guida. Oh, inizia la lezione!

gloss.en: I work in a museum, I'm a guide. Oh, the lesson is starting!
gloss.ko: 나는 박물관에서 일해, 가이드야. 앗, 수업 시작한다!

me-easy.text: Lavoro in un museo. Adesso c'è lezione.

gloss.en: I work in a museum. Now there's the lesson.

from-me.text: Io sono di Napoli, ma lavoro qui in un museo. Oh, inizia la lezione!

gloss.en: I'm from Naples, but I work here in a museum. Oh, the lesson is starting!
gloss.ko: 나는 나폴리 출신인데 여기 박물관에서 일해. 앗, 수업 시작한다!

gloss.en: For me too! See you later!

setting: A friend's flat in Turin on a Sunday afternoon. The tutor is Giulia, a friend, who is looking at a photo on the learner's phone: the learner's younger sister and a dog.

goal.en: Say she's your younger sister.
Say you have one sister and one brother.
goal.ko: 자매 하나, 형제 하나가 있다고 하세요.

expect.meaning: says how many siblings they have
match: ho una sorella e un fratello

goal.en: Say no, it's your sister's dog.

expect.meaning: says it belongs to the sister
match: è il cane di mia sorella

goal.en: Tell her the dog's name.

expect.meaning: does not know or did not understand

goal.en: Say yes, you like dogs a lot.

hello.text: Che bella foto! Chi è questa ragazza?

gloss.en: What a nice photo! Who is this girl?

hello-easy.text: Chi è? Questa ragazza, chi è?

gloss.en: Who is it? This girl, who is she?

you.text: Ah, sei tu! E la ragazza accanto a te?

gloss.en: Ah, it's you! And the girl next to you?
gloss.ko: 아, 너구나! 그럼 옆에 있는 여자애는?

sister.text: Che carina! Hai altri fratelli o sorelle?

gloss.en: How sweet! Do you have other brothers or sisters?
Do you have brothers? Sisters?

me.text: Io ho due fratelli, tutti e due più grandi. E questo cane? È tuo?

gloss.en: I have two brothers, both older. And this dog? Is it yours?
gloss.ko: 나는 오빠가 둘 있어. 그럼 이 개는? 네 개야?

gloss.en: And the dog? Is it yours?

hers.text: Ah, è di tua sorella! Come si chiama?

gloss.en: Ah, it's your sister's! What's its name?

yours.text: Ah, è tuo! Come si chiama?

gloss.en: Ah, it's yours! What's its name?
The dog's name?

like.text: Che nome simpatico! Ti piacciono i cani?

gloss.en: What a fun name! Do you like dogs?

like-easy.text: Ti piacciono i cani? Sì o no?

gloss.en: Do you like dogs? Yes or no?

end-yes.text: Anch'io! Dai, fammi vedere altre foto.

gloss.en: Me too! Come on, show me more photos.

end-cats.text: Ah, i gatti! Anch'io ho un gatto, guarda.

gloss.en: Ah, cats! I have a cat too, look.
gloss.ko: 아, 고양이! 나도 고양이 있어, 봐 봐.

setting: An aperitivo at a bar in the Navigli area of Milan, early evening. The tutor is Davide, a new friend from the learner's course. Small snacks come with the drinks.

goal.en: Say what drink you'd like.
Say you don't like olives.
Ask what they are.
Say you really like pasta.
Say yes, you'd love to.

hello.text: Allora, cosa prendi? Io prendo uno spritz.

gloss.en: So, what are you having? I'm having a spritz.
What are you having to drink?

noalc.text: Nessun problema, c'è anche il succo o l'acqua tonica. Ecco gli stuzzichini! Ti piacciono le olive?

gloss.en: No problem, there's juice or tonic water too. Here are the snacks! Do you like olives?
gloss.ko: 괜찮아, 주스나 토닉워터도 있어. 안주 왔다! 올리브 좋아해?

olives.text: Buona scelta. Ecco gli stuzzichini! Ti piacciono le olive?

gloss.en: Good choice. Here are the snacks! Do you like olives?
gloss.ko: 좋은 선택이야. 안주 왔다! 올리브 좋아해?

gloss.en: Olives: do you like them?

no-olives.text: Peccato, allora le mangio io! E questi, li conosci?

gloss.en: Too bad, then I'll eat them! And these, do you know them?
gloss.ko: 아쉽다, 그럼 내가 먹을게! 이건 알아?

yes-olives.text: Anche a me! E questi, li conosci?

gloss.en: Me too! And these, do you know them?
And these? Do you know them?

grissini.text: Sono grissini, sono di Torino. Senti, a te cosa piace mangiare?

gloss.en: They're grissini, they're from Turin. Listen, what do you like to eat?
gloss.ko: 그리시니야, 토리노 거야. 근데 너는 뭐 먹는 거 좋아해?

grissini-yes.text: Esatto, grissini! Senti, a te cosa piace mangiare?

gloss.en: Exactly, grissini! Listen, what do you like to eat?
gloss.ko: 맞아, 그리시니! 근데 너는 뭐 먹는 거 좋아해?

gloss.en: What do you like? Pasta? Pizza?

me.text: A me piace tutto! Soprattutto la pasta. Dai, la prossima volta andiamo a mangiare insieme?

gloss.en: I like everything! Especially pasta. Come on, shall we go eat together next time?
gloss.ko: 난 다 좋아! 특히 파스타. 다음에 같이 밥 먹으러 갈래?

pasta.text: Anche a me! Dai, la prossima volta andiamo a mangiare insieme?

gloss.en: Me too! Come on, shall we go eat together next time?
gloss.ko: 나도! 다음에 같이 밥 먹으러 갈래?

gloss.en: Shall we eat together? Yes?
Perfect! Cheers, then!

end-maybe.text: Va bene, ci pensi. Intanto cin cin!

gloss.en: OK, think about it. Cheers for now!

setting: A weekend outdoor club meeting at a lakeside park in Desenzano on Lake Garda, Saturday morning. The tutor is Paolo, a club member, who welcomes the learner on their first day.

goal.en: Say hi and tell him your name.

expect.meaning: only says yes, they are new

goal.en: Say yes, you can swim a little.
goal.ko: 네, 조금 수영할 줄 안다고 하세요.

goal.en: Say you don't speak English well.
Say you like riding a bike.
Say yes, you'll come.

hello.text: Ciao! È la prima volta nel gruppo? Io sono Paolo.

gloss.en: Hi! Is it your first time in the group? I'm Paolo.
gloss.ko: 안녕! 모임에 처음 왔어? 나는 파올로야.

hello-easy.text: Io sono Paolo. E tu come ti chiami?

gloss.en: I'm Paolo. And what's your name?

name.text: Piacere! Ti piace il lago? Sai nuotare?

gloss.en: Nice to meet you! Do you like the lake? Can you swim?
gloss.ko: 반가워! 호수 좋아해? 수영할 줄 알아?

gloss.en: Welcome! What's your name?
Do you swim? Yes or no?

swim-yes.text: Brava! Qui ci sono molti stranieri. Parli inglese?

gloss.en: Good for you! There are lots of foreigners here. Do you speak English?
gloss.ko: 잘하네! 여기 외국인 많아. 영어 할 줄 알아?

swim-no.text: Non c'è problema, facciamo anche altre cose. Parli inglese?

gloss.en: No problem, we do other things too. Do you speak English?
gloss.ko: 괜찮아, 다른 것도 해. 영어 할 줄 알아?

gloss.en: English: do you speak it?

eng-no.text: Non importa, parliamo italiano! E cosa ti piace fare?

gloss.en: Never mind, let's speak Italian! And what do you like doing?
gloss.ko: 괜찮아, 이탈리아어로 하자! 뭐 하는 거 좋아해?

eng-yes.text: Perfetto! Ma qui parliamo italiano. E cosa ti piace fare?

gloss.en: Perfect! But here we speak Italian. And what do you like doing?
gloss.ko: 좋아! 그래도 여기선 이탈리아어로 해. 뭐 하는 거 좋아해?

do-easy.text: Cosa ti piace? La bici? Camminare?

gloss.en: What do you like? Cycling? Walking?

bike.text: Che bello! Sabato facciamo un giro in bici. Vieni?

gloss.en: Great! On Saturday we're going on a bike ride. Are you coming?
gloss.ko: 좋다! 토요일에 자전거 타러 가. 올래?

me.text: Io amo la bici! Sabato facciamo un giro in bici. Vieni?

gloss.en: I love cycling! On Saturday we're going on a bike ride. Are you coming?
gloss.ko: 나는 자전거 좋아해! 토요일에 자전거 타러 가. 올래?

gloss.en: Saturday, by bike. Are you coming?
Perfect, see you on Saturday then!
Too bad! Next time, then.

setting: The coffee machine in a small office in Milan at 8:45 a.m. The tutor is Sara, a colleague, chatting before work starts.

goal.en: Say you get up at seven.
Say you have a meeting at ten.

expect.meaning: has a meeting or a lot of work

goal.en: Say you have lunch at one.
Say yes, gladly.

hello.text: Buongiorno! Già qui? Ma a che ora ti alzi?

gloss.en: Good morning! Here already? What time do you get up?
gloss.ko: 좋은 아침! 벌써 왔어? 몇 시에 일어나?

hello-easy.text: A che ora ti alzi la mattina?

gloss.en: What time do you get up in the morning?

early.text: Presto! Io mi alzo alle otto. Oggi hai tanto lavoro?

gloss.en: Early! I get up at eight. Do you have a lot of work today?
gloss.ko: 일찍 일어나네! 나는 여덟 시에 일어나. 오늘 일 많아?

gloss.en: Today: a lot of work or a little?

meeting.text: Ah, la riunione con il capo! In bocca al lupo. A che ora pranzi?

gloss.en: Ah, the meeting with the boss! Good luck. What time do you have lunch?
gloss.ko: 아, 팀장님이랑 회의! 잘해. 점심은 몇 시에 먹어?

little.text: Beata te! A che ora pranzi?

gloss.en: Lucky you! What time do you have lunch?
Lunch: what time?

together.text: Anch'io! Pranziamo insieme? C'è un bar qui sotto.

gloss.en: Me too! Shall we have lunch together? There's a bar downstairs.
gloss.ko: 나도! 같이 먹을까? 아래층에 바가 있어.

dunno.text: Allora pranziamo insieme all'una? C'è un bar qui sotto.

gloss.en: Then shall we have lunch together at one? There's a bar downstairs.
gloss.ko: 그럼 한 시에 같이 먹을까? 아래층에 바가 있어.

gloss.en: Shall we eat lunch together? Yes?

where.text: È qui sotto, a destra dell'ingresso. Allora, vieni?

gloss.en: It's downstairs, to the right of the entrance. So, are you coming?
gloss.ko: 바로 아래층, 입구 오른쪽이야. 그래서, 올래?

gloss.en: Perfect, see you later! Have a good day at work.

end-no.text: Va bene, un'altra volta. Buon lavoro!

gloss.en: OK, another time. Have a good day at work!

setting: The entrance hall of an apartment building in Padua, early evening. The tutor is Signora Bruni, an older neighbour who meets the learner for the first time by the letterboxes.

goal.en: Greet her politely and say yes.
Say where you work: an office.
Say yes, you like it a lot.
Ask if there's a supermarket near here.

match: sì, c'è un supermercato qui vicino?
scusi, c'è un supermercato qui vicino?

goal.en: Thank her for the information.

hello.text: Buonasera! Lei abita al terzo piano? È qui da poco?

gloss.en: Good evening! Do you live on the third floor? Have you just arrived?
gloss.ko: 안녕하세요! 4층(이탈리아식 3층)에 사세요? 이사 온 지 얼마 안 됐어요?

gloss.en: Good evening. Are you new here?

work.text: Piacere, io sono la signora Bruni. Lei lavora qui a Padova?

gloss.en: Nice to meet you, I'm Mrs Bruni. Do you work here in Padua?
gloss.ko: 반가워요, 나는 브루니예요. 여기 파도바에서 일해요?

gloss.en: Do you work here? Where do you work?

job.text: Ah, che bello! E le piace il quartiere?

gloss.en: Oh yes, on Saturdays there's the market. Do you need anything around here?

Ask how much a kilo of lemons costs.

gloss.en: Oranges, Sicilian oranges! Yes, what can I get you?

gloss.en: Two euros a kilo. How many would you like?
One kilo? Two kilos?

gloss.en: Here you are. Anything else? The lemons are excellent today.

gloss.en: Three euros. One kilo, three euros.

goal.ko: 진열장의 납작한 빵을 가리키며 뭔지 물어보세요.

goal.en: Ask politely for one piece.

goal.en: You don't know the word: ask how you say 'cookie' in Italian.
goal.ko: 단어를 몰라요. 'cookie'를 이탈리아어로 뭐라고 하는지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: asks how to say the word

come si dice questo in italiano?

goal.en: Say yes, two please.
Pay and say thank you.

gloss.en: Good morning! Go ahead.
Good morning. What would you like?

gloss.en: It's Genoese focaccia, with oil and salt. It's just been made!
gloss.ko: 제노바식 포카치아예요, 올리브유랑 소금. 방금 구웠어요!

focaccia-no.text: No, non è pizza: è focaccia genovese, con olio e sale.

gloss.en: No, it's not pizza: it's Genoese focaccia, with oil and salt.

gloss.en: It's focaccia. Bread with oil.

piece-price.text: Due euro al pezzo. Ne vuole uno?

gloss.en: Two euros a piece. Would you like one?
One piece? Two pieces?

sweet.text: Ecco qua. Vuole anche questi? Sono canestrelli, molto buoni.

gloss.en: Here you go. Would you like these too? They're canestrelli, very good.
gloss.ko: 여기요. 이것도 드릴까요? 카네스트렐리예요, 아주 맛있어요.

gloss.en: And these sweets? Do you want them?

gloss.en: You say 'biscotto'. Canestrelli are biscuits. Would you like some?
Biscotto. Bis-cot-to. Would you like some?

total.text: Allora, sono quattro euro in tutto.

gloss.en: So, that's four euros altogether.
Four euros, please.
Thank you, have a good day!

goal.en: Pay and thank them.

gloss.en: Good afternoon! Here's the menu. What can I bring you?
What are you eating today?

Carbonara, amatriciana or lasagne.

To drink? Water? Wine?
Still or sparkling?

gloss.en: Normal water or with bubbles?

gloss.en: Perfect, coming right up.

after.text: Tutto bene? Desidera altro? Un caffè, un dolce?

gloss.en: Everything OK? Would you like anything else? A coffee, a dessert?
gloss.ko: 괜찮으셨어요? 더 필요한 거 있으세요? 커피나 디저트?

after-easy.text: Vuole un caffè? Sì o no?

gloss.en: Do you want a coffee? Yes or no?

Here's the coffee.

bill.text: Sono quindici euro, con il coperto.

gloss.en: That's fifteen euros, with the cover charge.
Fifteen euros. One, five: fifteen.

gloss.en: The cover charge is for the bread and the table: two euros.
Thank you! Goodbye.

expect.meaning: asks about the bus to the museum
match: scusi, quale autobus va al museo?
quale autobus per il museo archeologico?

goal.en: You didn't catch the number. Ask her to repeat it.

match: può ripetere il numero, per favore?

Thank her for the help.

gloss.en: Ugh, the bus never comes today...
Yes? Go ahead.
For the museum? Take the 168.

gloss.en: Number one hundred sixty-eight. One, six, eight.

when.text: Arriva tra dieci minuti, più o meno.

gloss.en: It comes in about ten minutes.
Ten minutes. In ten minutes.

gloss.en: No, you buy the ticket at the tobacconist, over there.

Do you have another question?

gloss.en: Nine euros eighty. Almost ten euros.

time-easy.text: Alle dieci e venti. Binario sei.

Say you'll take it.

price-easy.text: Quarantacinque euro, con lo sconto meno.

gloss.en: Forty-five euros, less with the discount.

gloss.en: What have you lost? A bag? A phone?

what-lost.text: Ho capito. Cosa ha perso, esattamente?

gloss.en: I see. What exactly have you lost?
A backpack. What colour?
Black? Blue? Red?

gloss.en: And when did you lose it? On which train?
Today? Yesterday? At what time?
What's inside?
Inside the backpack: what is there?

gloss.en: One moment... No, I'm sorry, it isn't here yet. Come back tomorrow after ten.

goal.en: Thank them for the map.

gloss.ko: 안녕하세요, 시에나에 오신 걸 환영해요! 도와드릴까요?

gloss.ko: 자, 두오모, 만자 탑, 그리고 박물관이 많아요.

Your name?

hello.text: Ciao! Benvenuti in palestra. Vuoi fare l'iscrizione?

gloss.en: Hi! Welcome to the gym. Do you want to sign up?
gloss.ko: 안녕! 헬스장에 온 걸 환영해. 등록하려고?

gloss.en: Hi. Do you want to sign up?

month.text: Cinquanta euro al mese. Lavori qui in zona? C'è uno sconto.

gloss.en: Fifty euros a month. Do you work around here? There's a discount.
gloss.ko: 한 달에 50유로야. 이 근처에서 일해? 할인이 있어.

month-easy.text: Cinquanta euro, un mese. Lavori qui vicino?

gloss.en: Fifty euros, one month. Do you work near here?
Where do you work?

gloss.en: Perfect, then it's forty euros. What do you want to do? Weights, swimming, yoga?
gloss.ko: 좋아, 그럼 40유로야. 뭐 하고 싶어? 웨이트, 수영, 요가?

nodiscount.text: Va bene, cinquanta euro. Cosa vuoi fare? Pesi, nuoto, yoga?

gloss.en: OK, fifty euros. What do you want to do? Weights, swimming, yoga?
gloss.ko: 그래, 50유로. 뭐 하고 싶어? 웨이트, 수영, 요가?

gloss.en: Yoga? Swimming? Weights?

yoga.text: Lo yoga è il martedì e il giovedì alle sette.

gloss.en: Yoga is on Tuesday and Thursday at seven.
Tuesday and Thursday, at seven.

hours.text: Siamo aperti dalle sei alle ventidue.

gloss.en: We're open from six to ten p.m.

hours-easy.text: Dalle sei di mattina alle dieci di sera.

gloss.en: From six in the morning to ten at night.
Here's your card. See you!

setting: The reception desk of a small medical clinic (poliambulatorio) in Bari, morning. The tutor is the receptionist. The learner has an appointment and it is their first visit.

goal.en: Say good morning and that you have an appointment.
goal.ko: 아침 인사를 하고 예약이 있다고 하세요.

match: sì, ho un appuntamento con la dottoressa

goal.en: Tell them your name.
Say yes, it's your first time.
Say you don't understand that word.
Say OK, you understand now.
Say yes, here it is.
Thank them.

expect.meaning: asks how long the wait is

hello.text: Buongiorno. Ha un appuntamento?

gloss.en: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?
Appointment: yes or no?

name.text: Bene. Il suo nome, per favore?

gloss.en: Good. Your name, please?
What's your name?

first.text: Eccola, alle dieci con la dottoressa Russo. È la prima volta qui?

gloss.en: Here you are, at ten with Dr Russo. Is it your first time here?

first-easy.text: È la prima volta? Sì o no?

gloss.en: Is it the first time? Yes or no?
Then you need to fill in this form.
Write here: name, address, phone.

gloss.en: The form is this sheet. Write your name, address and phone number.

The health card: do you have it?

wait.text: Va bene. Si accomodi, la chiamiamo noi.

gloss.en: All right. Please take a seat, we'll call you.
You're welcome. See you shortly.

setting: The staircase of an old apartment building in Trieste, Sunday morning. The tutor is Signor Rossi, an elderly neighbour coming down with his newspaper.

goal.en: Greet him politely: it's morning.
Tell him your name.
Say you live on the third floor.
Say which city you're from.

goal.en: Say goodbye: see you soon.

hello.text: Oh, buongiorno! Non ci conosciamo, vero?

gloss.en: Oh, good morning! We haven't met, have we?

gloss.en: Are you new? I'm Mr Rossi.

name.text: Io sono Rossi, del primo piano. Lei come si chiama?

gloss.en: I'm Rossi, from the first floor. What's your name?
Your name?

floor.text: Piacere! E lei a che piano abita?

gloss.en: Nice to meet you! And which floor do you live on?
Which floor? Second? Third?

from.text: Ah, al terzo, sopra la signora Bruni! E lei di dov'è?

gloss.en: Ah, on the third, above Mrs Bruni! And where are you from?
gloss.ko: 아, 브루니 부인 위층이네요! 어디서 왔어요?

gloss.en: Where are you from? Which city?

korea.text: Che bello, così lontano! Benvenuti a Trieste. Adesso vado a prendere il caffè.

gloss.en: How nice, so far away! Welcome to Trieste. I'm going for a coffee now.
gloss.ko: 멀리서 왔네요! 트리에스테에 온 걸 환영해요. 나는 커피 마시러 가요.

gloss.en: Welcome! I'm going to the bar.
Goodbye, and have a nice Sunday!

setting: A language-exchange evening in a café in Perugia, near the University for Foreigners. The tutor is Luca, an Italian student who wants to learn Korean.

goal.en: Say yes and tell him your name.
Say you speak Korean and a little English.

match: parlo coreano e un po' di inglese
il coreano e un po' l'inglese

Ask how you say 'cheers' in Italian.

sì! come si dice cheers in italiano?

goal.en: Teach him the Korean word.

gloss.en: Hi! Are you here for the language exchange? I'm Luca.
gloss.ko: 안녕! 언어 교환하러 왔어? 나는 루카야.

gloss.en: Hi, I'm Luca. What's your name?
gloss.ko: 안녕, 나는 루카야. 너는 이름이 뭐야?

gloss.ko: 반가워! 무슨 언어 할 줄 알아?

gloss.en: Do you speak Korean? English?

Chinese? Yes or no?

gloss.en: What do you want to learn? Italian?

word.text: Allora facciamo così: io ti insegno l'italiano e tu mi insegni il coreano. Una parola?

gloss.en: Let's do this: I teach you Italian and you teach me Korean. A word?
gloss.ko: 이렇게 하자. 내가 이탈리아어 가르쳐 주고 너는 한국어 가르쳐 줘. 단어 하나?

gloss.en: Do you have a word to ask?

cheers.text: Si dice «cin cin»! E in coreano?

gloss.en: You say 'cin cin'! And in Korean?

cheers-easy.text: Cin cin. In coreano come si dice?

gloss.en: Cin cin. How do you say it in Korean?

end.text: «Geonbae»! Bellissimo. Allora cin cin, e geonbae!

gloss.en: 'Geonbae'! Lovely. Cheers, then, and geonbae!

setting: An Italian language class at a school in Florence, mid-lesson. The tutor is Elena, the classmate sitting next to the learner. The learner's pen has run out.

goal.en: Say yes, that's fine, and thank her.

gloss.en: A pencil? Here. Or do you want a pen?

gloss.en: The teacher said 'compiti'. I mean, the work to do at home.
gloss.ko: 선생님이 '콤피티'라고 했어. 집에서 할 숙제 말이야.

gloss.en: Compiti: the work for home.

end-class.text: Ok, la lezione è finita. Ti serve ancora la penna?

gloss.en: OK, the lesson's over. Do you still need the pen?

setting: Outside Bologna Centrale station, early evening. The learner is meeting their friend Matteo but they can't find each other, so Matteo calls on the phone. It is noisy with traffic.

Say you can see a bus stop.
It's noisy: ask him to repeat, please.
You don't know that place. Ask where it is.
Say OK, you see it.

gloss.en: Hello? Hi! I'm in front of the station. Where are you?
gloss.ko: 여보세요? 안녕! 나 역 앞이야. 너 어디야?

gloss.en: Where are you now?
Sorry, it's noisy! Where are you?

gloss.ko: 바 근처? 여기 바가 세 개야! 뭐가 보여?

gloss.en: What do you see? A shop? A bus?

gloss.en: Ah, the bus stop! OK, wait there, I'll be there in two minutes.

gloss.en: The edicola: the little newspaper shop, next to the stop.
gloss.ko: 에디콜라, 정류장 옆 작은 신문 가게야.

gloss.en: See you there. OK?

end.text: Perfetto! Ti vedo! A tra poco!

gloss.en: Perfect! I can see you! See you in a moment!

setting: The entrance of a design office in Milan at 9 a.m. The tutor is Federico, a friendly colleague arriving at the same time. They use tu.

goal.en: Say yes, good idea.
Say you'd like a cappuccino.
Say at one o'clock.

hello.text: Ehi, buongiorno! Come va?

gloss.en: Hey, good morning! How's it going?
Hi! All good?

good.text: Bene! Io un po' stanco. Ieri sera c'era la partita.

gloss.en: Good! I'm a bit tired. There was the match last night.
gloss.ko: 다행이다! 나는 좀 피곤해. 어제 저녁에 경기가 있었거든.

tired.text: Anch'io sono stanco! Ieri sera c'era la partita.

gloss.en: I'm tired too! There was the match last night.
gloss.ko: 나도 피곤해! 어제 저녁에 경기가 있었거든.

gloss.en: Shall we have a coffee before we start?
gloss.ko: 시작하기 전에 커피 한 잔 할까?

Coffee or cappuccino?

gloss.ko: 그래, 그럼 이따 봐. 오늘 점심 몇 시에 먹어?

end.text: Perfetto, anch'io! Pranziamo insieme. A dopo!

gloss.en: Perfect, me too! Let's have lunch together. See you later!
gloss.ko: 좋아, 나도! 같이 먹자. 이따 봐!

end-dunno.text: Ok, scrivimi un messaggio. Buon lavoro!

gloss.en: OK, send me a message. Have a good day at work!

Do you need help?

Which city? Where are you going?

Not at all! Have a good trip.

gloss.en: I'm going home too. Do you live far?

gloss.en: Nice! I'm going home. Do you live far?

At seven? Yes?
